hold_text: ⚠️ THE TOKEN IS IMPERFECT AND IS DISCLOSED AS SUCH, the way mi102's and mi95's were — read this before treating it as an operator quote, because NO OPERATOR SAID ANYTHING ABOUT THIS PR. The dispatching manager in fact told this session the opposite: to self-land as Tier-1 with both .github/pr-landing/{slug}.json and .github/pr-automerge-requests/{slug}.txt. That instruction cannot be followed, and the refusal is this guard's own: R5 refuses to self-land a diff containing .gitattributes, which is outside TIER1_SURFACE. So the thing actually asking for a hold is pr-landing-guard, whose R5 text says in as many words 'set landing: hold and let a human read it'. That is the instruction being honoured here, quoted from the guard rather than from a person. operator_asked_to_hold is the nearest of the five closed-vocabulary reasons and it is still not the right one: the vocabulary has no entry for 'Tier-1 work on a path the allowlist cannot vouch for', which is what this is. Filed as BL-20260905-PR-LANDING-VOCAB-HAS-NO-UNVOUCHED-PATH-HOLD. changes_landing_machinery was considered and rejected rather than skipped: R8 verifies it against LANDING_MACHINERY, .gitattributes is not in that list, so claiming it would fail the check and would also be a claim I cannot support. WHAT THE HUMAN IS BEING ASKED TO READ: one added mapping line, `docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl merge=union`, plus the comment recording why jsonregister was measured and rejected. TIER-1 BY THE CANONICAL DOC, NOT BY MY ASSERTION: docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md § Permission Tiers lists 'repo hygiene' and 'CI and lint configuration' as Tier-1 examples, and TIER1_SURFACE already carries the sibling root config files .ruff.toml, ruff.toml and pyproject.toml. .gitattributes' absence from that list looks like an oversight rather than a decision — but I have NOT widened the allowlist to say so, because editing the guard that judges my own PR is the exact 'cheaper to lie to than to satisfy' failure check_pr_landing.py's own docstring warns about. A human decides that, not me.
why: Merge-policy metadata plus one test. The whole diff is .gitattributes (one merge=union mapping for docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl and the measurement comment behind it), tests/ops/test_pending_pings_merge_union.py, and two health-review-backlog rows appended via backlog_append.py::append_row. No src/, no config/, no deploy/, no workflow, no order path, no live-VM file, no VM mutation. A git merge driver is CLIENT-SIDE ONLY — GitHub does not run it — so nothing GitHub executes changes, and a clone that ignores it merges exactly as it does today. union is a git built-in and needs no installer.
